source_ref: OSF v2zur (CC BY 4.0, node licence checked via api.osf.io 2026-09-28): W1 from 'C19PRC Study Waves 1 and 2' zip (md5 ca7c20869f574eb595e1f8e6e193fc84) -> C19PRC_UKW1W2_archive_final.sav variable+value labels for W1_Conspiracy_1-5, cross-checked against 'C19PRC_UKW1 survey questionnaire.pdf' Q93 (block 'Conspiracy mentality (Bruder 2014)', pp.33-35, image-only PDF read visually); W4 from 'C19PRC-UKW4 OSF.zip' (osf.io/download/jhqty, md5 278242af9dd75b4e5fafadea4eb7ce99) -> C19PRC_UK_W4_archive_final.sav labels for W4_Conspiracy_1-5 and C19PRC_UK_W4_Recontacts/Oversamples questionnaire.pdf block 'Conspiracy' (p.107 / p.119)
note: Item codes Conspiracy_1..5 are the .sav column names W1_/W4_Conspiracy_N with the wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key cmq; number-preserving, no positional step, no reverse-coding). The W1 and W4 .sav variable labels are identical strings for all 5 items ('I think that...... - <statement>'); the shared stem 'I think that......' went to instructions and the statement to item_text, 5/5 verbatim incl. the leading ellipsis character and item 3's missing final full stop. Value labels identical in W1 and W4 for all 5 items: 1='Certainly not 0%', 2..5='10%'..'40%', 6='Undecided 50%', 7..10='60%'..'90%', 11='Certainly 100%' (the questionnaire grid headers read the same). Wording caveat: at W4 the grid was preceded by an extra framing question (Q628: 'We are also interested in understanding some of your personal beliefs. For each of the statements below, please use the respective rating scale to indicate how likely it is in your opinion that the statement is true. Remember that there are no “objectively” right or wrong answers and that we are interested in your personal opinion.'); W1 had no such text (block begins directly with 'Q93 I think that......'). Since items are pooled across waves, only the text common to both waves is shipped in instructions. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): per-wave x item x resp counts from the two .sav files match the live table cell-for-cell, 110/110 (W1 n=2025 per item, W4 n=3867 per item; 29460 rows, 4621 ids); every item uses all 11 levels. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv row CMQ = ship (Bruder et al. 2013 Front Psychol, CC BY); administered wording matches the register's match_item_text for all 5 items. Deposit CC BY 4.0.

note: Item codes are the .sav column names W3_Comfort_* with the W3_ wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key comfort; no positional step, codes self-describing). The .sav variable labels read '<Q358 stem> - <activity>'; the shared stem went to instructions and the activity to item_text, 9/9 identical to the Phase 1 questionnaire Q358 row labels. Only whitespace was normalised: every variable label carries a line break after 'Compared', collapsed to a single space. option_text = the .sav value labels 1=Not at all comfortable, 2=Somewhat comfortable, 3=Very comfortable, 4=Completely comfortable (identical for all 9 items, matching the questionnaire column headers). Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per-item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 36/36 (e.g. Comfort_MeetOutside 213/637/213/103, Comfort_LargeEvent 845/187/87/47); live table is wave 3 only, 10494 rows, 1166 ids. Q358 appears in the W3 Phase 1 questionnaire and not in the Phase 2 questionnaire; the .sav has 853 respondents with all nine items missing. Study-specific ad hoc items, not a named published instrument; no rights-holder restriction beyond the deposit's CC BY 4.0.
